verdict.rationale: Phoenix documents official, first-party SDKs. Its Python SDK is modular, with installable packages and an API reference covering auto-instrumentation, tracing decorators and span querying. Python and TypeScript SDKs exist for running evaluations, and client SDKs keep prompts in sync across environments. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of building against the SDKs, and documented TypeScript SDK coverage beyond evaluations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Phoenix's Python SDK is modular by design, allowing you to install only what you need. Each package serves a specific purpose and can be used independently or together.
Python and TypeScript SDKs for running evaluations against Phoenix traces, datasets, or any data source. Full control over evaluation logic, judge models, and pipelines.
Phoenix offers client SDKs to keep your prompts in sync across different applications and environments.
Tracing decorators — @tracer.chain, @tracer.tool, and more for manual instrumentation
